season_info.banner_message: It is currently September. In Cần Thơ, this is the Mùa season. The best time to plant is now — here are your recommendations.

notes: Soil pH within optimal range (5.0–7.5) — no pH adjustment needed

applications.method: Band application 5 cm below and to the side of the seed row to avoid fertiliser burn.
Side-dress along crop rows at 15 cm depth. Cultivate lightly to incorporate. Irrigate after if no rain within 48 h.
Top-dress between rows or foliar spray. Keep off leaves in high temperatures to reduce burn risk.

general_notes: Never apply all nitrogen at once — split into at least 3 applications to reduce losses.
Irrigate after each application if no significant rain (≥ 10 mm) is expected within 48 hours.
Wear gloves when handling — avoid inhaling fertiliser dust.

land_preparation: Plough to 20–25 cm. Ridge planting recommended on lower-lying clay loam fields.
Apply 2 t/ha compost before final tillage to improve aeration.
planting: Plant at start of rainy season. Drainage is critical — avoid low-lying fields for Mùa maize.
Direct sow 2–3 seeds per hill at 5 cm depth; row spacing: 70 cm; hill spacing: 25 cm.
⚠ 12 rainy days forecast — if soil is waterlogged, delay planting by 5–7 days. Saturated soil at planting increases damping-off and root rot risk.
water_management: Maize requires 500–700 mm total water over the full growing season.
Most critical stage: silking (days 55–70). Water stress at silking reduces final yield by 30–50%.
Check soil moisture by pressing a handful of soil — if it crumbles and does not form a ball, irrigate.
pest_watch: Fall armyworm: scout weekly from week 2 throughout Mùa season.
Stem rot and downy mildew are elevated risks in Mùa wet conditions — ensure good field drainage.

irrigation_schedule.note: Critical for uniform emergence; waterlogging at germination causes damping-off
30–50 mm per irrigation event; adjust based on daily rainfall
Most critical stage — water stress here permanently reduces yield by 30–50%
Reduce frequency as grain hardens; excess moisture at this stage risks lodging
Stop 2–3 weeks before harvest to allow dry-down for mechanised harvesting

harvest_timing.reason: No major climate risks detected for the harvest window. Harvest at the start of the optimal window for the best balance of maturity and field-loss risk.
harvest_tips: Harvest when husks are dry brown and kernel moisture is around 25–28%.
Shell cobs within 2 days to prevent mould in humid conditions.
Target moisture content: 25% at harvest, dry to 13% for safe storage.
harvest_timing.data_basis: Historical climate NASA POWER 2025 average for this province

season_info.banner_message: It is currently September. In Đắk Lắk, this is the annual season. The best time to plant is now — here are your recommendations.

notes: High rainfall forecast — reduced N by 15% to limit leaching
Soil pH within optimal range (5.0–7.5) — no pH adjustment needed

applications.method: Broadcast under canopy within the drip zone and water in. For young trees, apply in a ring at half the drip radius.
Broadcast and allow rain to incorporate. Avoid application in waterlogged conditions.
Apply potassium-heavy blend to build reserves before the dry season.

general_notes: Young trees (< 3 years): apply at 50% of recommended rate.
Do not apply nitrogen immediately before or during flowering — it can reduce fruit set.
Wear gloves when handling — avoid inhaling fertiliser dust.

land_preparation: Dig planting holes 50 × 50 × 50 cm. Backfill with topsoil + 3 kg compost per hole.
Minimal tillage beyond hole preparation — cashew develops a deep taproot; avoid mechanical disturbance.
planting: Plant grafted seedlings at the start of the dry season — taproots establish before rains arrive.
Spacing: 7 × 7 m (200 trees/ha) or 10 × 10 m (100 trees/ha) for mechanised harvest operations.
Plant 1 seedling per prepared hole; backfill firmly and stake if site is exposed to wind.
⚠ 11 rainy days forecast — if soil is waterlogged, delay planting by 5–7 days. Saturated soil at planting increases damping-off and root rot risk.
water_management: Mature cashew (>3 years old) is drought-tolerant and rarely requires irrigation.
Young trees (year 1–2): irrigate every 10–14 days during dry months (December–April).
No irrigation needed from June–October when rainy season provides sufficient moisture.
pest_watch: Tea mosquito bug (Helopeltis spp.): main pest at leaf flushing and flowering. Spray neem extract or approved pyrethroid weekly during these stages.
Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides): inspect new shoots for brown-black lesions. Apply copper-based fungicide at bud break and repeat after 14 days.
Stem and root borer: check base of trunk for entry holes and sawdust deposits. Apply chlorpyrifos solution to the trunk base as a preventive measure.

irrigation_schedule.note: Irrigate until new leaf flush is confirmed — indicates successful root establishment
Stop irrigation entirely during rainy season; drought-tolerant once established
Dry conditions promote heavier and more uniform flowering
One supplemental irrigation during nut sizing improves kernel weight by 10–15%
Rainy season provides sufficient moisture; supplemental irrigation not needed

harvest_timing.reason: Tropical storm season peaks in September in this region. Harvesting 5 days before the optimal window reduces weather-loss risk. Yield penalty estimated at 3–5%.

climate_risks.action: Harvest by Nov 17 to avoid late-season storm risk (peak storm months in this region: September, October, November).
Wet harvest conditions likely. Plan mechanical drying capacity or covered storage. Harvest early morning when humidity is lowest.

harvest_tips: Harvest fallen nuts daily — ground contact causes rapid quality deterioration.
The cashew apple is highly perishable; process or sell within 24 h.
Target 8–9% moisture for raw cashew nuts in storage.
harvest_timing.data_basis: Historical climate NASA POWER 2025 average for this province
